name: Spirits and Liqueurs

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will learn basics of spirit and liqueur production including the base ingredients, flavors, and location of production for important spirits of the world.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will gain a deeper knowledge in spirits and liqueurs of the world by understand the region, styles, raw materials, aging requirements, and the general production process. A Certified Sommelier will be able to recommend spirits and liqueurs to guests and will know the base spirits, mixers, and garnishes for selected cocktails.

rows.intro: Vodka: Anywhere in the world; Rum: Can be anywhere but traditionally Caribbean; Gin: Anywhere in the world
Rum: Light, Dark, Aged, Spiced; Gin: London Dry
Vodka: Commonly cereal grain but can be anything; Rum: Sugarcane and Molasses; Gin: Neutral Grain
Vodka: Commonly continuous still; Rum: Continuous or pot still; Gin: Continuous
Vodka: Multiple times in continuous still to remove any flavors; Gin: Flavored with botanicals and Juniper berries.

rows.certified: Vodka: Tito's, Absolut, Smirnoff, Stolichnaya, Grey Goose, Kettle One, Cîroc, Belvedere; Rum: Myers's, Mount Gay, Bacardi, Captain Morgan (Spiced), Diplomático, Goslings, Havana Club; Gin: Tanqueray, Bombay, Nolet, Beefeater, Hendrick's, Sipsmith
Tequila: Blanco: under 2 months; Reposado: 2 months to 1 year in oak; Añejo: 1 year to 3 years in oak; Mezcal: Blanco (most common), Reposado, Añejo

rows.intro: Tequila: Blue Agave; Mezcal: Agave (many varieties)
Tequila: Continuous or pot still; Mezcal: Continuous or pot still

Scotch Whisky: Highland, Lowland, Islay (Smokiest), Speyside, Campbeltown; Unheaded column: Blended Scotch
